subject: math
title: Coordinate Geometry
syllabus: Cartesian system of rectangular coordinates in a plane, distance formula, section formula, locus and its equation, the slope of a line, parallel and perpendicular lines, intercepts of a line on the coordinate axis. Straight line: various forms of equations of a line, intersection of lines, angles between two lines, conditions for concurrence of three lines, the distance of a point from a line, coordinates of centroid, orthocentre, and circumcentre of a triangle. Circle, conic sections: a standard form of equations of a circle, the general form of the equation of a circle, its radius and centre, equation of a circle when the endpoints of a diameter are given, points of intersection of a line and a circle with the centre at the origin and sections of conics, equations of conic sections (parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola) in standard forms.

body: Slope m = \f{y_{2} − y_{1}}{x_{2} − x_{1}}. Parallel lines share m; perpendicular lines have m_{1}m_{2} = −1.
Distance of (x_{1}, y_{1}) from ax + by + c = 0 is \f{|ax_{1} + by_{1} + c|}{√{a^{2} + b^{2}}}. Between parallel lines: \f{|c_{1} − c_{2}|}{√{a^{2} + b^{2}}}.
Image of a point in a line: move twice the signed distance along the normal (a, b).
Centroid G = average of the vertices. Incentre = \f{aA + bB + cC}{a + b + c} (a, b, c = opposite side lengths).
Orthocentre H: meet of altitudes. Circumcentre O: meet of perpendicular bisectors. G lies on OH with OG : GH = 1 : 2.
In a right triangle, H is the right-angle vertex and O is the mid-point of the hypotenuse.
x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has centre (−g, −f) and radius √{g^{2} + f^{2} − c}.
A line at distance d from the centre: cuts if d < r (chord 2√{r^{2} − d^{2}}), touches if d = r.
Tangent length from P: √{S(P)}. Two circles: subtract the equations to get the common chord / radical axis.
Touching circles: |C_{1}C_{2}| = r_{1} + r_{2} (external) or |r_{1} − r_{2}| (internal).
y^{2} = 4ax: focus (a, 0), directrix x = −a, latus rectum 4a. Every point is as far from the focus as from the directrix.
Parametric point (at^{2}, 2at). A focal chord joins t and −\f{1}{t}; its length is a(t + \f{1}{t})^{2}.
Tangent of slope m: y = mx + \f{a}{m}, touching at (\f{a}{m^{2}}, \f{2a}{m}).
Chord with mid-point (h, k): T = S_{1}, slope \f{2a}{k}.
Latus rectum \f{2b^{2}}{a}. For any point, PS + PS' = 2a and focal distances are a ± ex.
y = mx + c touches when c^{2} = a^{2}m^{2} + b^{2}.
|PS − PS'| = 2a; focal distances ex ± a. Latus rectum \f{2b^{2}}{a}.
y = mx + c touches when c^{2} = a^{2}m^{2} − b^{2}. Rectangular hyperbola xy = c^{2}: point (ct, \f{c}{t}), e = √2.

traps: Write the line as ax + by + c = 0 before using the distance formula — watch the sign of c.
Radius needs g^{2} + f^{2} − c > 0; otherwise there is no real circle.
Internal touching uses the difference of radii, not the sum.
For y^{2} = 4ax, a is a quarter of the coefficient of x.
In an ellipse a is the larger semi-axis — check whether the major axis is along y.
Ellipse: b^{2} = a^{2} − c^{2}; hyperbola: c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}. Don't mix them.

pyq.q: Let the area of the triangle formed by a straight line L : x + by + c = 0 with co-ordinate axes be 48 square units. If the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the line L makes an angle of 45° with the positive x-axis, then the value of b^{2} + c^{2} is :
sol: The foot of the perpendicular is along 45°, so the normal (1, b) is along (1, 1): b = 1 and L is x + y = −c.

pyq.q: Let the three sides of a triangle are on the lines 4x − 7y + 10 = 0, x + y = 5 and 7x + 4y = 15. Then the distance of its orthocentre from the orthocentre of the triangle formed by the lines x = 0, y = 0 and x + y = 1 is
sol: 4x − 7y + 10 = 0 and 7x + 4y = 15 are perpendicular, so the orthocentre is their meeting point (1, 2).
The other triangle is right-angled at O. Distance from (1, 2) to (0, 0) = √{5}.

pyq.q: Let two straight lines drawn from the origin O intersect the line 3x + 4y = 12 at the points P and Q such that △OPQ is an isosceles triangle and ∠POQ = 90°. If l = OP^{2} + PQ^{2} + QO^{2}, then the greatest integer less than or equal to l is :
sol: The altitude from O is the distance to the line: h = \f{12}{5}. The legs are h√{2}, the hypotenuse 2h.

pyq.q: If P(6, 1) be the orthocentre of the triangle whose vertices are A(5, −2), B(8, 3) and C(h, k), then the point C lies on the circle.
sol: AP ⊥ BC: h + 3k = 17. BP ⊥ AC: h + k = 3.

pyq.q: Let a variable line of slope m > 0 passing through the point (4, −9) intersect the coordinate axes at the points A and B. The minimum value of the sum of the distances of A and B from the origin is ____.

Let ABC be the triangle such that the equations of lines AB and AC be 3y − x = 2 and x + y = 2, respectively, and the points B and C lie on x-axis. If P is the orthocentre of the triangle ABC, then the area of the triangle PBC is equal to
sol: A = (1, 1), B = (−2, 0), C = (2, 0). Altitude from A is x = 1; altitude from B ⊥ AC is y = x + 2.

pyq.q: A line passing through the point P(a, 0) makes an acute angle α with the positive x-axis. Let this line be rotated about the point P through an angle \f{α}{2} in the clock-wise direction. If in the new position, the slope of the line is 2 − √{3} and its distance from the origin is \f{1}{√{2}}, then the value of 3a^{2} tan^{2}α − 2√{3} is
sol: New slope tan \f{α}{2} = 2 − √{3} → α = 30°. The new line through (a, 0) has distance |a| sin 15° = \f{1}{√{2}} from O.

pyq.q: If the image of the point (−4, 5) in the line x + 2y = 2 lies on the circle (x + 4)^{2} + (y − 3)^{2} = r^{2}, then r is equal to :

If the orthocentre of the triangle formed by the lines 2x + 3y − 1 = 0, x + 2y − 1 = 0 and ax + by − 1 = 0, is the centroid of another triangle, whose circumcentre and orthocentre respectively are (3, 4) and (−6, −8), then the value of |a − b| is ____.
sol: Centroid divides OH in 1 : 2 from the circumcentre: G = \f{2(3, 4) + (−6, −8)}{3} = (0, 0).
So the orthocentre is the origin: the altitude through (−1, 1) forces a = −b, and the one through the vertex on 2x + 3y = 1 gives b = 8 → |a − b| = 16.

pyq.q: Two vertices of a triangle ABC are A(3, −1) and B(−2, 3), and its orthocentre is P(1, 1). If the coordinates of the point C are (α, β) and the centre of the circle circumscribing the triangle PAB is (h, k), then the value of (α + β) + 2(h + k) equals :
sol: AP ⊥ BC and BP ⊥ AC give C = (21, 26).
The circumcentre of PAB has h + k = −21, so (21 + 26) + 2(−21) = 5.

pyq.q: A variable line L passes through the point (3, 5) and intersects the positive coordinate axes at the points A and B. The minimum area of the triangle OAB, where O is the origin, is :
Let the mid points of the sides of a triangle ABC be (\f{5}{2}, 7), (\f{5}{2}, 3) and (4, 5). If its incentre is (h, k), then 3h + k is equal to :
Let the triangle PQR be the image of the triangle with vertices (1, 3), (3, 1) and (2, 4) in the line x + 2y = 2. If the centroid of △PQR is the point (α, β), then 15(α − β) is equal to :
sol: The image of the centroid is the centroid of the image: reflect (2, \f{8}{3}).

pyq.q: Let the distance between two parallel lines be 5 units and a point P lie between the lines at a unit distance from one of them. An equilateral triangle PQR is formed such that Q lies on one of the parallel lines, while R lies on the other. Then (QR)^{2} is equal to ____.
sol: Take the lines y = 0, y = 5 and P(0, 1); Q = (q, 0) rotated 60° about P must land on y = 5.

pyq.q: Let the area of a △PQR with vertices P(5, 4), Q(−2, 4) and R(a, b) be 35 square units. If its orthocenter and centroid are O(2, \f{14}{5}) and C(c, d) respectively, then c + 2d is equal to
sol: PQ is horizontal of length 7, so |b − 4| = 10; the altitude from R is vertical through the orthocentre: a = 2.
Only b = −6 puts the orthocentre at (2, \f{14}{5}). Centroid (\f{5}{3}, \f{2}{3}) → c + 2d = 3.

pyq.q: Let ^{n}C_{r−1} = 28, ^{n}C_{r} = 56 and ^{n}C_{r+1} = 70. Let A(4 cos t, 4 sin t), B(2 sin t, −2 cos t) and C(3r − n, r^{2} − n − 1) be the vertices of a triangle ABC, where t is a parameter. If (3x − 1)^{2} + (3y)^{2} = α, is the locus of the centroid of triangle ABC, then α equals
sol: 3x − 1 = 4 cos t + 2 sin t, 3y = 4 sin t − 2 cos t → sum of squares 16 + 4 = 20.

pyq.q: The absolute difference between the squares of the radii of the two circles passing through the point (−9, 4) and touching the lines x + y = 3 and x − y = 3, is equal to ____.
sol: The centre is on a bisector of the two lines: y = 0 (the bisector x = 3 gives no real circle). Centre (h, 0), radius \f{|h − 3|}{√{2}}.

pyq.q: Let C be a circle with radius √{10} units and centre at the origin. Let the line x + y = 2 intersects the circle C at the points P and Q. Let MN be a chord of C of length 2 unit and slope −1. Then, a distance (in units) between the chord PQ and the chord MN is
sol: PQ is at distance √{2} from O. A chord of length 2 is at distance √{10 − 1} = 3.

pyq.q: A square is inscribed in the circle x^{2} + y^{2} − 10x − 6y + 30 = 0. One side of this square is parallel to y = x + 3. If (x_{i}, y_{i}) are the vertices of the square, then Σ(x_{i}^{2} + y_{i}^{2}) is equal to :
sol: Centre (5, 3), radius 2. The vertices are the centre ± two perpendicular radius vectors.

pyq.q: Let the circle C_{1} : x^{2} + y^{2} − 2(x + y) + 1 = 0 and C_{2} be a circle having centre at (−1, 0) and radius 2. If the line of the common chord of C_{1} and C_{2} intersects the y-axis at the point P, then the square of the distance of P from the centre of C_{1} is :
sol: C_{2}: x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x − 3 = 0. Subtracting: common chord 2x + y = 2.
It meets the y-axis at (0, 2): distance^{2} from (1, 1) = 2.

pyq.q: Let a circle C of radius 1 and closer to the origin be such that the lines passing through the point (3, 2) and parallel to the coordinate axes touch it. Then the shortest distance of the circle C from the point (5, 5) is :
sol: Touching x = 3 and y = 2 with radius 1: centre (3 ± 1, 2 ± 1); nearest to O is (2, 1).
Distance from (5, 5) to (2, 1) is 5 → shortest distance 5 − 1 = 4.

pyq.q: Let the line 2x + 3y − k = 0, k > 0, intersect the x-axis and y-axis at the points A and B, respectively. If the equation of the circle having the line segment AB as a diameter is x^{2} + y^{2} − 3x − 2y = 0 and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x^{2} + 9y^{2} = k^{2} is \f{m}{n}, where m and n are coprime, then 2m + n is equal to
sol: The circle on AB as diameter: x^{2} + y^{2} − \f{k}{2}x − \f{k}{3}y = 0 → k = 6.

pyq.q: A circle in inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side of length 12. If the area and perimeter of any square inscribed in this circle are m and n, respectively, then m + n^{2} is equal to ____.
sol: Inradius = \f{12}{2√{3}} = 2√{3}; the square's diagonal is the diameter 4√{3}.

pyq.q: Let C_{1} be the circle in the third quadrant of radius 3, that touches both coordinate axes. Let C_{2} be the circle with centre (1, 3) that touches C_{1} externally at the point (α, β). If (β − α)^{2} = \f{m}{n}, gcd(m, n) = 1, then m + n is equal to
sol: C_{1}: centre (−3, −3). The contact point is 3 units from it towards (1, 3): direction \f{(4, 6)}{2√{13}}.

pyq.q: Let r be the radius of the circle, which touches x-axis at point (a, 0), a < 0 and the parabola y^{2} = 9x at the point (4, 6). Then r is equal to ____.
sol: The centre (a, r) lies on the normal at (4, 6) (slope −\f{4}{3}) and is r away from (4, 6).

pyq.q: Let the circles C_{1} : (x − α)^{2} + (y − β)^{2} = r_{1}^{2} and C_{2} : (x − 8)^{2} + (y − \f{15}{2})^{2} = r_{2}^{2} touch each other externally at the point (6, 6). If the point (6, 6) divides the line segment joining the centres of the circles C_{1} and C_{2} internally in the ratio 2 : 1, then (α + β) + 4(r_{1}^{2} + r_{2}^{2}) equals

Consider the circle C : x^{2} + y^{2} = 4 and the parabola P : y^{2} = 8x. If the set of all values of α, for which three chords of the circle C on three distinct lines passing through the point (α, 0) are bisected by the parabola P is the interval (p, q), then (2q − p)^{2} is equal to ____.
sol: Midpoint (h, k) with k^{2} = 8h; the chord hx + ky = h^{2} + k^{2} passes through (α, 0) → α = h + 8.
Three chords need h > 0 inside the circle: h^{2} + 8h < 4 → α ∈ (8, 4 + 2√{5}) → (8 + 4√{5} − 8)^{2} = 80.

pyq.q: Let the centre of a circle, passing through the point (0, 0), (1, 0) and touching the circle x^{2} + y^{2} = 9, be (h, k). Then for all possible values of the coordinates of the centre (h, k), 4(h^{2} + k^{2}) is equal to ____.
sol: h = \f{1}{2} (the centre is on the perpendicular bisector of (0, 0), (1, 0)); r = √{\f{1}{4} + k^{2}}.
Internal touching: |OC| = 3 − r and |OC| = r → r = \f{3}{2} → 4(h^{2} + k^{2}) = 4r^{2} = 9.

pyq.q: Let the circle x^{2} + y^{2} = 4 intersect x-axis at the points A(a, 0), a > 0 and B(b, 0). Let P(2 cos α, 2 sin α), 0 < α < \f{π}{2} and Q(2 cos β, 2 sin β) be two points such that (α − β) = \f{π}{2}. Then the point of intersection of AQ and BP lies on
sol: AQ ⊥ BP? Use angles: the intersection sees AB at a fixed angle of 45°, so it lies on a fixed circle through A and B.
Checking points: the locus is x^{2} + y^{2} − 4y − 4 = 0.

pyq.q: Let a circle pass through the origin and its centre be the point of intersection of two mutually perpendicular lines x + (k − 1)y + 3 = 0 and 2x + k^{2}y − 4 = 0. If the line x − y + 2 = 0 intersects the circle at the points A and B, then (AB)^{2} is equal to :
sol: Perpendicular: 2 + (k − 1)k^{2} = 0 → k = −1. The lines x − 2y + 3 = 0, 2x + y − 4 = 0 meet at (1, 2): r^{2} = 5.

pyq.q: A circle C of radius 2 lies in the second quadrant and touches both the coordinate axes. Let r be the radius of a circle that has centre at the point (2, 5) and intersects the circle C at exactly two points. If the set of all possible values of r is the interval (α, β), then 3β − 2α is equal to :
sol: C: centre (−2, 2). The centres are 5 apart; two meeting points need |r − 2| < 5 < r + 2.

pyq.q: The focus of the parabola y^{2} = 4x + 16 is the centre of the circle C of radius 5. If the values of λ, for which C passes through the point of intersection of the lines 3x − y = 0 and x + λy = 4, are λ_{1} and λ_{2}, λ_{1} < λ_{2}, then 12λ_{1} + 29λ_{2} is equal to ____.

Let circle C be the image of x^{2} + y^{2} − 2x + 4y − 4 = 0 in the line 2x − 3y + 5 = 0 and A be the point on C such that OA is parallel to x-axis and A lies on the right hand side of the centre O of C. If B(α, β), with β < 4, lies on C such that the length of the arc AB is (1/6)^{th} of the perimeter of C, then β − √{3}α is equal to
sol: The circle has centre (1, −2), radius 3; its image has centre (−3, 4).

pyq.q: Let the equation of the circle, which touches x-axis at the point (a, 0), a > 0 and cuts off an intercept of length b on y-axis be x^{2} + y^{2} − αx + βy + γ = 0. If the circle lies below x-axis, then the ordered pair (2a, b^{2}) is equal to

Let the focal chord PQ of the parabola y^{2} = 4x make an angle of 60° with the positive x axis, where P lies in the first quadrant. If the circle, whose one diameter is PS, S being the focus of the parabola, touches the y-axis at the point (0, α), then 5α^{2} is equal to :
sol: The chord y = √{3}(x − 1) meets y^{2} = 4x at x = 3 → P = (3, 2√{3}).
Circle on PS: centre (2, √{3}), radius 2 → touches the y-axis at (0, √{3}) → 5α^{2} = 15.

pyq.q: Let the point P of the focal chord PQ of the parabola y^{2} = 16x be (1, −4). If the focus of the parabola divides the chord PQ in the ratio m : n, gcd(m, n) = 1, then m^{2} + n^{2} is equal to :

The axis of a parabola is the line y = x and its vertex and focus are in the first quadrant at distances √{2} and 2√{2} units from the origin, respectively. If the point (1, k) lies on the parabola, then a possible value of k is :
sol: Vertex (1, 1), focus (2, 2): the directrix is x + y = 0.

pyq.q: A line passing through the point A(−2, 0), touches the parabola P : y^{2} = x − 2 at the point B in the first quadrant. The area, of the region bounded by the line AB, parabola P and the x-axis, is :
sol: B = (2 + t^{2}, t): the tangent slope \f{1}{2t} equals the slope of AB, \f{t}{t^{2} + 4} → t = 2, B = (6, 2).
Triangle under AB (area 8) minus the area under y = √{x − 2} from 2 to 6 (\f{16}{3}) = \f{8}{3}.

pyq.q: Let PQ be a chord of the parabola y^{2} = 12x and the midpoint of PQ be at (4, 1). Then, which of the following point lies on the line passing through the points P and Q?
sol: Chord with midpoint (h, k): T = S_{1} → y·1 − 6(x + 4) = 1 − 48 → y = 6x − 23.

pyq.q: Let the length of the focal chord PQ of the parabola y^{2} = 12x be 15 units. If the distance of PQ from the origin is p, then 10p^{2} is equal to ____.
sol: Focal chord at angle θ: length 4a cosec^{2}θ = \f{12}{sin^{2}θ} = 15 → sin^{2}θ = \f{4}{5}.
It passes through (3, 0): p = 3 sin θ → 10p^{2} = 72.

pyq.q: Let a line perpendicular to the line 2x − y = 10 touch the parabola y^{2} = 4(x − 9) at the point P. The distance of the point P from the centre of the circle x^{2} + y^{2} − 14x − 8y + 56 = 0 is ____.
sol: Slope −\f{1}{2}. For y^{2} = 4(x − 9) the tangent of slope m touches at (9 + \f{1}{m^{2}}, \f{2}{m}) = (13, −4).

pyq.q: Suppose AB is a focal chord of the parabola y^{2} = 12x of length l and slope m < √{3}. If the distance of the chord AB from the origin is d, then ld^{2} is equal to
sol: l = \f{12}{sin^{2}θ}, d = 3 sin θ (distance from O to the chord through (3, 0)).

pyq.q: Let L_{1}, L_{2} be the lines passing through the point P(0, 1) and touching the parabola 9x^{2} + 12x + 18y − 14 = 0. Let Q and R be the points on the lines L_{1} and L_{2} such that the △PQR is an isosceles triangle with base QR. If the slopes of the lines QR are m_{1} and m_{2}, then 16(m_{1}^{2} + m_{2}^{2}) is equal to ____.
sol: y = sx + 1 in the parabola: 9x^{2} + (12 + 18s)x + 4 = 0, tangent when 12 + 18s = ±12 → s = 0, −\f{4}{3}.
QR is perpendicular to a bisector of the angle at P: slopes 2 and −\f{1}{2} → 16(4 + \f{1}{4}) = 68.

pyq.q: Let P be the parabola, whose focus is (−2, 1) and directrix is 2x + y + 2 = 0. Then the sum of the ordinates of the points on P, whose abscissa is −2, is

Let A be the focus of the parabola y^{2} = 8x. Let the line y = mx + c intersect the parabola at two distinct points B and C. If the centroid of the triangle ABC is (\f{7}{3}, \f{4}{3}), then (BC)^{2} is equal to :
Let one end of a focal chord of the parabola y^{2} = 16x be (16, 16). If P(α, β) divides this focal chord internally in the ratio 5 : 2, then the minimum value of α + β is equal to :
sol: (16, 16) has t = 2; the other end has t = −\f{1}{2}: (1, −4).
The two ways of dividing 5 : 2 give α + β = 22 or 7 → minimum 7.

pyq.q: Let P(4, 4√{3}) be a point on the parabola y^{2} = 4ax and PQ be a focal chord of the parabola. If M and N are the foot of perpendiculars drawn from P and Q respectively on the directrix of the parabola, then the area of the quadrilateral PQMN is equal to :
sol: PQNM is a trapezium with parallel sides 7 and \f{21}{4}, height 7√{3} → \f{343√{3}}{8}.

pyq.q: If the line 3x − 2y + 12 = 0 intersects the parabola 4y = 3x^{2} at the points A and B, then at the vertex of the parabola, the line segment AB subtends an angle equal to
sol: They meet at x = 4 and −2: A(4, 12), B(−2, 3).
Slopes 3 and −\f{3}{2} from the origin; OA·OB > 0 so the angle is acute: tan θ = \f{9}{7}.

pyq.q: If S and S' are the foci of the ellipse \f{x^{2}}{18} + \f{y^{2}}{9} = 1 and P be a point on the ellipse, then min(SP · S'P) + max(SP · S'P) is equal to :

Let one focus of the hyperbola H : \f{x^{2}}{a^{2}} − \f{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1 be at (√{10}, 0) and the corresponding directrix be x = \f{9}{√{10}}. If e and l respectively are the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of H, then 9(e^{2} + l) is equal to :
If the length of the minor axis of an ellipse is equal to one fourth of the distance between the foci, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :
A line passing through the point P(√{5}, √{5}) intersects the ellipse \f{x^{2}}{36} + \f{y^{2}}{25} = 1 at A and B such that (PA) · (PB) is maximum. Then 5(PA^{2} + PB^{2}) is equal to :
sol: PA · PB = \f{|S(P)|}{cos^{2}θ/36 + sin^{2}θ/25}, largest when the line is horizontal (θ = 0).

pyq.q: Let the product of the focal distances of the point P(4, 2√{3}) on the hyperbola H : \f{x^{2}}{a^{2}} − \f{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1 be 32. Let the length of the conjugate axis of H be p and the length of its latus rectum be q. Then p^{2} + q^{2} is equal to ____.

Let C be the circle of minimum area enclosing the ellipse E : \f{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \f{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1 with eccentricity \f{1}{2} and foci (±2, 0). Let PQR be a variable triangle, whose vertex P is on the circle C and the side QR of length 2a is parallel to the major axis of E and contains the point of intersection of E with the negative y-axis. Then the maximum area of the triangle PQR is :
sol: a = 4, b = 2√{3}; the smallest enclosing circle has radius a = 4. QR lies on y = −2√{3}.

pyq.q: If the equation of the hyperbola with foci (4, 2) and (8, 2) is 3x^{2} − y^{2} − αx + βy + γ = 0, then α + β + γ is equal to ____.
sol: Centre (6, 2), c = 2; the coefficients force b^{2} = 3a^{2}, so 4a^{2} = 4 → a^{2} = 1.

pyq.q: The length of the latus-rectum of the ellipse, whose foci are (2, 5) and (2, −3) and eccentricity is \f{4}{5}, is

Let for two distinct values of p the lines y = x + p touch the ellipse E : \f{x^{2}}{4^{2}} + \f{y^{2}}{3^{2}} = 1 at the points A and B. Let the line y = x intersect E at the points C and D. Then the area of the quadrilateral ABCD is equal to :
sol: y = x meets E at ±(\f{12}{5}, \f{12}{5}). Shoelace on A, C, B, D gives 24.

pyq.q: The centre of a circle C is at the centre of the ellipse E : \f{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \f{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1, a > b. Let C pass through the foci F_{1} and F_{2} of E such that the circle C and the ellipse E intersect at four points. Let P be one of these four points.
